claims.claim_ar: الجذر أمن: يحمل دلالة الاطمئنان/الإيمان؛ الفعل آمَنُوا (ماضي/فعل ماضٍ مع واو الجماعة) بمعنى «آمنوا/صدقوا بالإيمان»
claims.claim_en: Root 'أمن' (amn) carries the semantic field of security/assurance and belief; the form آمَنُوا is the perfect (past) third-person plural of the Form I verb meaning 'they believed'/'they were secure in belief'.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source contains the verb (آمن) in a prose explanation but does not give an explicit morphological paradigmatization for the exact form آمَنُوا.

claims.claim_ar: أَصْدَقُ على وزن أفعل (اسم تفضيل/أفعل) من الجذر صدق؛ هنا يعمل كاسم تفضيل/استفهام إنكاري بمعنى «أَجْدَرُ بِالصِّدقِ/أَشَدُّ صِدقاً»
claims.claim_en: The word 'أَصْدَقُ' is on the af‘al (أفعل) pattern (an elative/comparative form) from the root ṣ-d-q meaning 'truth/being truthful'. In this context it functions as a comparative/elative ('more truthful' / 'truest'), rendered in the verse as 'Who is more truthful than Allah in speech?'.

claims.claim_ar: ضدّ الصدق: الكذب (الكذب مذكور كنقيض للصدق في الشرح)
claims.claim_en: Antonym: the opposite of 'ṣidq' (truthfulness) is 'kidhb' (lying). The commentary explicitly contrasts truth with lying ('lying is not applicable to Him').
claims.needs_review_reason: The source passage contrasts truth and lying in a theological commentary (about Allah); the antonym relation is semantic rather than an explicit morphological statement about the word's pattern.

claims.source_quote_ar: لأنه عز وعلا صادق لا يجوز عليه الكذب.
claims.claim_ar: اسم الله موصوف بالصِدق: «لا يجوز عليه الكذب» — تصفيفة دلالية لاسم الله تفيد الصدق المطلق كخاصية إلهية
claims.claim_en: The Divine Name 'Allah' is described as 'ṣādiq' (truthful); the commentary states 'lying does not befit Him', giving a theological/semantic property (antonymic relation to lying).
